title: Channel-scoped archive reads leak other channels whose names start with it (read -c dev --all sweeps dev-hotfix)
desc: DEFECT, reproduced on current main. fetch_messages filters archive files by a bare prefix: name.startswith(ch + '-'). Archive files are '<channel>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>.jsonl', and '-' is legal inside channel names, so a read of channel 'dev' also matches the archive of channel 'dev-hotfix'. Reproduced in a --local repo with two channels of 600 messages each, rotate, then: `read -c dev --all --jsonl` returned 1080 messages — 600 [dev] + 480 [dev-hotfix]. Control: `read -c dev-hotfix --all` returns its own 600, 0 leaked (one-directional). Impact: cross-channel leakage of archived messages into any channel-scoped archive read (read --all is the user-facing path; also any future consumer), i.e. task channels or private-ish channels bleed into broader ones. ACCEPTANCE: (1) match the archive's timestamp shape, not a bare prefix: file must equal ch + '-' + <8digit>T<6digit>Z + '.jsonl' (read-path only, no renaming, no data-layout change, R10 — there are no archives on main yet, so no legacy names to honour); (2) new stdlib test tests/test_archive_channel_scope.py: red on main (the 480 leaked), green after, and it also pins that (a) the channel's OWN archive is still included (600 = 120 hot + 480 archived), (b) the all-channels read still returns every message from both channels (1200), so the fix drops nothing; (3) full suite green.
